cards.name: Reduce Interlace Flicker
cards.summary: Applies a small vertical-only blur to calm the line twitter / flicker of thin horizontal detail (fine text, stripes, venetian blinds) on interlaced or downscaled output. On progressive footage it simply softens vertically.
use_for: Calm shimmering thin horizontal lines in a lower-third or ticker made for an interlaced broadcast (1080i) delivery
Stop moire / twitter on scanned documents, newspaper clippings or spreadsheets zoomed in an explainer
Soften striped shirts or blinds that buzz after heavy downscaling of a 4K news clip
avoid: Using it as a general blur: it blurs only vertically, so values well above 10 build into a vertical smear that reads as a broken deinterlace, not a defocus
Leaving it on progressive web deliveries (Reels, YouTube) where there is no flicker to fix: it just costs sharpness

params.name: Softness
params.does: Amount of vertical blur used to suppress line flicker
params.typical: 0.5-1.5 for flicker fixes; 0 = off. Range 0-1000. On a 1080p sequence 10 is only about a 4 px vertical blur (barely visible full-frame); larger values build into a visible vertical smear

cards.scripting: Single number property 'Softness' (0..1000 clamp, useful 0-3). The demo value 50 is deliberately exaggerated so the vertical softening is visible in a test frame (10 rendered as only a ~4 px vertical blur plus a ~5 px upward shift on 1080p, invisible full-frame); real use is 0.5-1.5, which is invisible on a still. Apply to the graphic, ticker or document clip (after any scaling), not to the whole sequence via an adjustment layer, so faces stay sharp. Folder placement (Blur & Sharpen vs Video) in the v26 Effects panel is not verified.

verified.note: Softness 50 gives a strong vertical-only smear (horizontal edges like block tops and stripes soften, vertical edges stay), as described.

cards.name: Find Edges
cards.summary: Detects high-contrast edges and draws them as dark, colour-tinted lines on a white field (or bright coloured lines on black when inverted), giving a pencil-sketch or line-art version of the shot.
use_for: Sketch-to-photo reveal on a key press photo in a documentary (animate Blend With Original from sketch to real)
Line-art background behind a quote card or explainer graphic so text reads clearly
Inverted neon-outline look for a trailer or reel transition beat
Stylised 'case file' treatment of archival stills in a political explainer
avoid: Noisy, low-light or heavily compressed footage: grain becomes a mess of speckled lines
Holding it for long on faces: people read as harsh and unflattering

params.name: Invert
params.does: false = dark lines on white (sketch); true = bright lines on black (neon/blueprint)
params.typical: false for sketch, true for neon outlines

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back the original image; harvest clamps this to 0-1, so it is a fraction (UI shows %)
params.typical: 0 for full sketch, 0.3-0.6 for a tinted sketch-over-photo

cards.scripting: Blend With Original is 0..1 here (unlike Invert / Lens Flare where it is 0..100): send 0.5 for 50%, not 50. Default (Invert false, Blend 0) already gives the full effect. Add Tint or Lumetri after it to colour the lines; add a light blur before it on noisy footage.

verified.note: Whole shot becomes dark, slightly colour-tinted edge lines on a white field, a clear pencil-sketch look.

cards.name: Four-Point Garbage Matte
cards.summary: Cuts the clip to a four-cornered polygon defined by four corner points; everything outside becomes transparent. Used to crop away rigs, edges or unwanted areas, often before keying.
use_for: Remove a light stand, boom or studio edge from a green-screen anchor shot before Ultra Key
Cut a TV screen, phone or banner out of a shot so another clip on a lower track shows through
Make an angled or trapezoid picture-in-picture panel for a news split screen
Trim a black border, letterbox edge or frame-edge artefact off an archival or screen-recorded clip with an angled cut
avoid: Moving subjects crossing the matte edge: the edge is hard (no feather) and points are not tracked
Leaving any point unset: harvested defaults all read [0, 0], which can collapse the matte and make the clip vanish

params.name: Top Left
params.does: Top-left corner of the kept area, frame fraction

params.name: Top Right
params.does: Top-right corner

params.name: Bottom Right
params.does: Bottom-right corner

params.name: Bottom Left
params.does: Bottom-left corner

cards.equivalent: Opacity mask in Premiere for feathered shapes; AE: layer mask (no effect equivalent)
cards.scripting: Always set all four points explicitly: the harvest read every default as [0, 0] (in the UI they start at the frame corners), so a script that sets only some points may get a degenerate matte. Points are frame fractions and may go outside 0..1. Outside area is transparent, so put a background clip on a lower track or it shows black. No feather control on the matte edge: use an opacity mask with feather when a soft edge is needed. In After Effects the same job is done with a layer mask, not an effect.

verified.note: Image is cropped to a tilted four-corner polygon at the demo points; everything outside is transparent (black).

cards.name: Sixteen-Point Garbage Matte
cards.summary: Same as the four-point garbage matte but with sixteen points (corner vertices plus intermediate edge points) for a more detailed polygon cutout; everything outside becomes transparent.
use_for: Rough-cut around an irregular studio set or rig before keying an anchor
Isolate an oddly shaped screen, poster or podium in a press-event shot
Cut a shaped panel (rounded or angled) for a split-screen debate layout
avoid: Animated subjects: sixteen points are tedious to keyframe and the edge is hard; use a feathered mask instead
Leaving points at the harvested [0, 0] default: the matte collapses

params.name: Top Left Vertex
params.does: Top-left corner point of the polygon (frame fraction); the 16 points run clockwise from here in the order listed

params.name: Top Left Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the top edge (Top Left Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Top Center Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the top edge (Top Center Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Top Right Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the top edge (Top Right Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Right Top Vertex
params.does: right top corner point of the polygon (frame fraction)

params.name: Right Top Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the right edge (Right Top Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Right Center Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the right edge (Right Center Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Right Bottom Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the right edge (Right Bottom Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Bottom Right Vertex
params.does: bottom right corner point of the polygon (frame fraction)

params.name: Bottom Right Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the bottom edge (Bottom Right Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Bottom Center Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the bottom edge (Bottom Center Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Bottom Left Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the bottom edge (Bottom Left Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Left Bottom Vertex
params.does: left bottom corner point of the polygon (frame fraction)

params.name: Left Bottom Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the left edge (Left Bottom Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Left Center Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the left edge (Left Center Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

params.name: Left Top Tangent
params.does: intermediate polygon point on the left edge (Left Top Tangent); a straight-line point, not a curve handle

cards.equivalent: Opacity mask in Premiere for feathered shapes; AE: layer mask (no effect equivalent)
cards.scripting: Set all 16 points: harvest defaults are [0, 0] for every point. The points run clockwise in the harvested order (Top Left Vertex, Top Left Tangent, Top Center Tangent, Top Right Tangent, Right Top Vertex, ... Left Top Tangent); despite the name 'Tangent' they are ordinary polygon points joined by straight lines, which is what the demo assumes (medium confidence). Points are frame fractions. Outside is transparent.

verified.note: Image is cut to a 16-point hard-edged polygon with points pushed out at each side centre; outside is transparent.

cards.name: Eight-Point Garbage Matte
cards.summary: An eight-point polygon cutout (four corner vertices plus four edge mid points); everything outside the shape becomes transparent.
use_for: Rough garbage matte around a green-screen presenter before Ultra Key
Cut out a bevelled or angled panel for a news split screen or picture-in-picture
Cut an irregular shape (e.g. a podium or a tilted screen) out of a press-event shot so a clip on a lower track shows through
avoid: Hard, unfeathered edge looks cheap on a visible cutout; add a border or shadow or use a mask with feather
Unset points default to [0, 0] and collapse the matte

params.name: Top Left Vertex
params.does: Top-left corner (frame fraction)

params.name: Top Center Tangent
params.does: Top edge mid point

params.name: Right Top Vertex
params.does: Top-right corner

params.name: Right Center Tangent
params.does: Right edge mid point

params.name: Bottom Right Vertex
params.does: Bottom-right corner

params.name: Bottom Center Tangent
params.does: Bottom edge mid point

params.name: Left Bottom Vertex
params.does: Bottom-left corner

params.name: Left Center Tangent
params.does: Left edge mid point

cards.equivalent: Opacity mask in Premiere for feathered shapes; AE: layer mask (no effect equivalent)
cards.scripting: Set all 8 points (harvest defaults are all [0, 0]). Order is clockwise from Top Left Vertex; the 'Tangent' points are straight-line polygon points on each edge mid. Frame-fraction coordinates; outside the polygon is transparent, so place a background on a lower track.

verified.note: Image is cut to an eight-sided hard-edged polygon (corners plus side mid points); outside is transparent.

cards.name: Gaussian Blur (Legacy)
cards.summary: The old Gaussian blur: smooth, even blur in both or one direction. Superseded by the newer Gaussian Blur effect; kept so old projects still open.
use_for: Only when an existing project already uses it: keep or tweak a blurred background plate behind explainer text (new work: Gaussian Blur)
Blur-in / blur-out between documentary stills in an old project (keyframe Blurriness)
One-direction blur (Blur Dimensions 1 or 2) for a fake motion streak, which the new Gaussian Blur does not offer as a dropdown
avoid: Building new edits on it: use the current Gaussian Blur
Repeat Edge Pixels off on full-frame clips: dark soft edges bleed in

params.name: Blurriness
params.does: Blur amount in pixels
params.typical: 10-40 for background plates, 60+ for full abstraction

params.name: Blur Dimensions
params.does: Direction: 0 both, 1 horizontal, 2 vertical

params.name: Repeat Edge Pixels
params.does: Keeps the frame edges from going soft/dark

cards.scripting: Obsolete: plan with 'Gaussian Blur' (the current effect) instead. If an old project already uses it: Blurriness 0..30000 (default 25), Blur Dimensions dropdown 0..2 (0 = Horizontal and Vertical), Repeat Edge Pixels bool default true.

verified.note: A frame exists despite the obsolete status: Blurriness 40 gives an even, clearly visible soft blur in both directions.

cards.name: Gradient Wipe
cards.summary: Makes the clip transparent pixel by pixel in order of brightness of a gradient source, as Transition Completion rises: dark areas of the gradient disappear first. With no gradient layer chosen it uses the clip's own luminance.
use_for: Luma-driven reveal of a clip on a lower track (shadows of the top clip vanish first) for a documentary scene change
Ink / smoke / paper-burn style transition using a gradient or texture clip on another track as the Gradient Layer (the layer has to be picked by hand in Effect Controls; a spec cannot set it)
Stylised reveal of a headline graphic or map in an explainer
avoid: Expecting a clean directional wipe: with the clip's own luminance it looks blotchy; use the Linear Wipe transition (or the Linear Wipe (Legacy) effect) for clean edges
Softness 0 on detailed footage gives a noisy, crunchy edge

params.name: Transition Completion
params.does: How far the wipe has progressed, 0-1 fraction

params.name: Transition Softness
params.does: Feathers the wipe edge, 0-1 fraction

params.name: Gradient Layer
params.does: Track/layer whose luminance drives the wipe (layer popup)
params.typical: leave default (clip itself) unless a gradient clip sits on another track

params.name: Gradient Placement
params.does: How a gradient layer of a different size is fitted: 0 tile, 1 centre, 2 stretch to fit

params.name: Invert Gradient
params.does: Bright areas disappear first instead of dark

cards.scripting: Transition Completion and Transition Softness are 0..1 fractions (send 0.5, not 50). Gradient Layer is a layer popup: harvested value 4294967294 with a nonsense range (min 3294967296 > max 1000000000), so do not set it from a spec; leave it on its default, which (medium confidence) makes the clip use its own luminance. To use a texture or gradient clip, the user must pick it in the UI. Transparent areas show the track below, so place the incoming clip underneath. Gradient Placement labels follow the After Effects order (Tile, Center, Stretch), default 2.

verified.note: At 50% completion the darker areas (clothing, shadows) have gone transparent/black while brighter areas remain, a luma wipe using the clip itself.

cards.name: Vector Motion
cards.category: Graphics (Essential Graphics component; not an Effects-panel effect)
cards.summary: The built-in transform of a Premiere graphic clip (Essential Graphics text and shapes): position, scale, rotation and anchor for the whole graphic, applied as vectors so it stays sharp at any scale. It is not an effect you add from the Effects panel.
use_for: Slow push-in on a title or lower-third graphic without softening the text
Reposition or rescale a whole Essential Graphics template for a 9:16 reel version
Animate a full graphic group (logo plus text) onto the frame in an explainer
avoid: Applying it to camera footage or stills: it belongs to graphic clips; use Motion or Transform for video
Scale above 100% on graphics that contain embedded raster images: those still soften

params.name: Position
params.does: Where the graphic's anchor sits, frame fraction

params.name: Scale
params.does: Uniform scale in percent

params.name: Scale Width
params.does: Horizontal scale in percent when Uniform Scale is off

params.name: Uniform Scale
params.does: Locks width to Scale

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Rotation in degrees

params.name: Anchor Point
params.does: Pivot for scale/rotation, frame fraction

cards.equivalent: Motion (the raster transform on every clip); AE: layer Transform with Continuously Rasterize on
cards.scripting: Exists only as a fixed component on graphic clips (Essential Graphics titles/shapes and many .mogrt templates); a script should find it on the graphic clip's components and set it, not add it to a video clip. Whether adding it to ordinary video does anything is untested (low confidence), hence status needs_input. Scale and Scale Width 0..10000 %, Rotation -32768..32767 degrees, Position/Anchor Point frame fractions.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input and no frame was rendered for it (no entry in the gallery index).

cards.name: Group
cards.category: Graphics (Essential Graphics component; not an Effects-panel effect)
cards.summary: The transform of a group of layers inside a Premiere graphic clip (layers grouped in the Essential Graphics panel): position, scale, rotation and anchor for just that group.
use_for: Animate a logo plus its tag line together inside a lower-third while other text stays put
Slide a grouped name strap in from the side for a news anchor super
Rescale one part of a template (e.g. a badge) for a vertical reel layout
avoid: Using it to move ordinary video: QE will add it to a video clip (the harvest did, all 6 properties appear) but whether it transforms footage is unverified; use Motion or Transform there

params.name: Position
params.does: Group position, frame fraction

params.name: Scale
params.does: Uniform scale in percent

params.name: Scale Width
params.does: Horizontal scale in percent when Uniform Scale is off

params.name: Uniform Scale
params.does: Locks width to Scale

params.name: Rotation
params.does: Rotation in degrees

params.name: Anchor Point
params.does: Pivot for scale/rotation, frame fraction

cards.equivalent: AE: parenting layers to a null, or a precomp's Transform
cards.scripting: A component Premiere creates when layers are grouped in a graphic; the reliable use is to look it up among an existing graphic clip's components (there may be several, one per group) and set it. QE addVideoEffect does add it to an ordinary video clip (harvest: no error, component 'Group' with these 6 properties), but its effect on footage there is unverified. Same property set and ranges as Vector Motion: Scale and Scale Width 0..10000 %, Rotation -32768..32767 degrees, Position/Anchor Point frame fractions.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input and no frame was rendered for it (no entry in the gallery index).
verified.second_opinion: corrected: card said Group is not addable to video clips; the harvest added it via QE to an ordinary video clip without error (pr_video_effects.json i=44), so avoid/scripting now say it is addable but its effect on footage is unverified. not_rendered verdict itself is right (needs_input, no gallery frame).

cards.name: Horizontal Flip
cards.summary: Mirrors the clip left to right. It has no controls.
use_for: Make a subject face into the frame / toward the text side in an explainer layout (only when no text is visible in the shot)
Match screen direction of a generic stock B-roll vehicle or walking shot so action reads continuously across a cut
Build a mirrored split-screen symmetry for a trailer beat (with a second copy unflipped)
avoid: Any shot with readable text, flags, party symbols, logos, number plates or watches: they appear reversed and look fake
News or political footage where flipping a real person could be seen as altering the record
Recognisable faces of known people: the mirror image looks subtly wrong to viewers
cards.equivalent: Transform (Scale Width -100) in After Effects, or layer Scale [-100, 100]
cards.scripting: No properties: apply with {"name": "Horizontal Flip", "pr_props": {}}; adding the effect is the flip, so demo_settings is necessarily empty and the flip is visible immediately. Cannot be keyframed; for an animated flip keyframe Basic 3D Swivel 0 to 180 instead (medium confidence that Premiere's Motion/Transform scale cannot go negative). In After Effects use Transform with Scale Width -100 (or the layer's own scale).

verified.note: Frame is mirrored left to right (right-hand content now on the left, left-hand content on the right).

cards.name: Invert
cards.summary: Inverts the colour information of the chosen channel (by default RGB, giving a photo-negative look). Other channel choices invert only hue, lightness, a single colour channel or alpha.
use_for: One- or two-frame negative flash on a beat hit in a reel or trailer
X-ray / film-negative treatment of archival stills in a documentary flashback
Invert a black-on-white document scan into white-on-black for a dark explainer layout
Flip a matte's alpha (Channel = Alpha) when a key or track matte is the wrong way round
avoid: Holding full RGB inversion on people for long: skin turns blue-green and looks alarming
Rapid repeated negative flashes: photosensitivity risk, keep flashes short and few

params.name: Channel
params.does: Which channel to invert (dropdown, 0-based; see enum_labels)
params.typical: 0 (RGB) for negative; 15 (Alpha) to flip a matte

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back the original, 0-100 percent
params.typical: 0 for full effect, 40-70 for a washed half-negative

cards.scripting: Channel range 0..15 matches the After Effects list with separators counted: 0 RGB, 1 Red, 2 Green, 3 Blue, 4 (separator), 5 HLS, 6 Hue, 7 Lightness, 8 Saturation, 9 (separator), 10 YIQ, 11 Luminance, 12 In Phase Chrominance, 13 Quadrature Chrominance, 14 (separator), 15 Alpha. 0 and 15 are near-certain; 5-13 are inferred from that layout (medium confidence). Never send 4, 9 or 14. Blend With Original is 0..100 here (unlike Find Edges, where it is 0..1). For a flash, keyframe Blend With Original rather than toggling the effect.

verified.note: Full RGB photo-negative: dark clothing turns white/cream, stripes and flowers invert to cyan/blue tones.

cards.name: Lens Flare
cards.summary: Renders a simulated camera lens flare (bright hotspot plus coloured ghost rings along a line through frame centre) over the clip, using one of three lens types.
use_for: Sun hit over a rally crowd or skyline establishing shot in a political documentary
Light sweep across a title or logo reveal in a trailer (animate Flare Center)
Add warmth / energy to a flat stock shot in a reel hook
Glint on a product, award or trophy shot
avoid: Flare placed where no light source exists in the shot: reads instantly fake
Brightness over ~150 on faces or text: blows them out and looks cheap
Overuse on news footage: it reads as stylised and editorialised

params.name: Flare Center
params.does: Position of the flare hotspot, frame fraction
params.typical: on a real light source, e.g. [0.8, 0.15] for sun top-right

params.name: Flare Brightness
params.does: Intensity in percent

params.name: Lens Type
params.does: Lens model (dropdown 0-2): changes ring pattern and size
params.typical: 0 (50-300mm Zoom) for the classic multi-ring flare; 1 and 2 give simpler ring patterns, compare visually

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back the original, 0-100 percent

cards.scripting: Flare Center is a frame-fraction point (default [0.4, 0.4]); Flare Brightness 0..300; Lens Type dropdown 0..2 (0 50-300mm Zoom, 1 35mm Prime, 2 105mm Prime, AE order); Blend With Original 0..100. The flare is drawn on the clip itself, so on a transparent clip it only appears where there are pixels: apply it to the footage, or to a black Color Matte on the track above with Blend Mode Screen so it can be moved and faded independently. Animating Flare Center across the frame gives the light-sweep reveal. Not the same as the newer Light Leaks, Glint or Volumetric Rays effects.

verified.note: Bright hotspot at top right (~0.78, 0.22) with coloured ghost rings along a line through the centre toward lower left.
